items.stem: Why does SDM let you *request* a subsite rather than create one directly?

options.text: The highest SPO permission delegated to SDM is 'Contribute', which can't create a subsite
Subsites are deprecated in SharePoint Online
SDM has no connection to SharePoint at all
Team Site owners are not allowed to have subsites

items.explanation: Creating a subsite needs elevated SPO privileges; SDM tops out at 'Contribute', which can't create one — so it offers a request instead.

misconceptions.b: The reason is a permission ceiling, not deprecation.
misconceptions.c: SDM does connect to SharePoint via the SPO sync; it just lacks creation rights.
misconceptions.d: Team Site owners can have subsites — they just request them here.

items.stem: After you submit a subsite request, when is the subsite actually created?

options.text: The next time the SPO sync runs
Immediately, as soon as you click submit
Only after an HRAD import completes
Never — SDM just stores the request for reporting

items.explanation: The request is fulfilled the next time the SharePoint Online sync runs, which has the elevated permissions SDM lacks.

misconceptions.b: It isn't instant — the page records a request that the sync later fulfills.
misconceptions.c: The SPO sync provisions the subsite, not an HRAD import.
misconceptions.d: The request is acted on: the SPO sync creates the subsite.

items.stem: A Team Site owner submits a subsite request and the subsite hasn't appeared a few minutes later. What is the most likely explanation?

options.text: The SPO sync hasn't run yet; the subsite is created on its next run
The request failed and must be re-submitted immediately
SDM created it but is hiding it until approval
Their account lost the 'Contribute' permission

items.explanation: This is a request-and-wait flow: the subsite is provisioned the next time the SPO sync runs, so a delay is expected, not a failure.

misconceptions.b: A delay is normal — re-submitting isn't the fix; the sync simply hasn't run.
misconceptions.c: SDM can't create the subsite at all; the sync does, when it runs.
misconceptions.d: The permission ceiling is exactly why a request is used; it's not the cause of the delay.

items.stem: Which statement best describes what the Subsites page actually does?

options.text: It queues a request that the SPO sync later turns into a real subsite
It creates the subsite live in SharePoint using SDM's admin rights
It deletes existing subsites from the Team Site
It edits HRAD school records that feed SharePoint

items.explanation: The page records a subsite request; the SharePoint Online sync, which has the elevated rights SDM lacks, creates the subsite on its next run.

misconceptions.b: SDM has no admin/creation rights in SPO — only 'Contribute'.
misconceptions.c: The page is about requesting creation, not deletion.
misconceptions.d: It concerns SharePoint subsites, not HRAD school records.

items.stem: Who is described as maintaining subsite creation and the related supplemental data?

options.text: Team Site owners
The HRAD system of record
The Help Desk only
Anyone with read-only SPO access

items.explanation: The tooltip states Team Site owners maintain subsite creation and their supplemental data — they submit the request and own the result.

misconceptions.b: HRAD is the source for staff/schools, not subsite requests.
misconceptions.c: This page is for Team Site owners, not a Help-Desk-only function.
misconceptions.d: Read-only access can't request a subsite; owners do.

items.stem: In one or two sentences, explain why SDM offers a subsite *request* instead of creating the subsite outright, and when the subsite finally gets created.
rubric: States SDM's highest delegated SPO permission is 'Contribute', which can't create a subsite
States the subsite is created the next time the SPO sync runs (request-and-wait, not instant)
items.sampleAnswer: Creating a subsite needs elevated SPO rights, but SDM only has 'Contribute', which can't create one — so it records a request instead. The subsite is actually provisioned the next time the SharePoint Online sync runs.
